Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Global Findex 2021 shows 36% of adults in Burkina Faso have an account (financial institution or mobile money) per World Bank Open Data series; this suggests active digital financial account usage in the 20-49% band.
revision_notes: Original comment cited account ownership (36%) as a proxy and linked to FX.OWN.TOTL.PL.ZS, which is actually the sub-indicator for adults with primary education or less, not the general population account-ownership series - a mismatched source. Fetched and read the official Global Findex 2021 country data table (Little Data Book on Financial Inclusion 2022, World Bank), which reports Burkina Faso's precise 'made or received a digital payment in the past year' figure (the closest available proxy to the variable definition) at 33.3% of adults, alongside account ownership of 36.1% (matching the general FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS series, most recently 51.43% for 2024). Both the account-ownership and the more directly relevant digital-payment figures fall within the 20-49% band, so the Value Code of 2 is confirmed. Attempted to source a precise 2024/2025 Findex figure for 'made or received digital payment' but the available PDF table's column alignment could not be read with confidence, so the verified 2021 figure is used as the safer, clearly-sourced basis; this should be revisited once a clean 2024/2025 country-level figure is available.
revised_comments: Global Findex data for 2021 indicate that 33.3% of adults (15+) in Burkina Faso made or received a digital payment in the past year, while 36.1% held an account at a financial institution or with a mobile-money provider. Both measures place active digital payment usage in the 20-49% band. Broader account ownership has since risen to 51.4% by 2024 per World Bank data, pointing to continued growth in digital financial inclusion, though a precise instant-payment-system-specific usage figure for the most recent year is not yet confirmed.
